KnowledgeArticle.Title: Street Light Complaint
KnowledgeArticle.Description: Report a problem with a street light.

Section.Name: 911 Street Light Complaint
Section.Content:
Call 911
Call 911 to report a downed power line.

Need something else?

  • Street Light Installation or Relocation Request to request a new street light or to have an existing street light relocated
  • Traffic Signal Complaint or Request
  • Pedestrian Signal Complaint or Request
  • Electrical Complaint to report dangling or hanging power lines
  • Light from Parking Lot Complaint
  • Service Request Status

You can report a problem with a street light to the Department of Transportation (DOT).

Section.Name: Report Street Light Conditions
Section.Content:
Street lights turn on at dusk. You can report street light conditions on all City roadways and pathways, including:

  • Highways
  • Streets
  • Paths in parks
  • Playgrounds
  • Parking lots in public parks
  • Golf courses

Street light conditions include:

  • On during the day
  • Burned out
  • Flickering/cycling on and off
  • Leaning pole
  • Exposed electrical wires in the base of the street light

DOT responds to most street light conditions within 10 days.

Street light outages due to nearby construction, ConEd power issues, an obstruction in the base, or where a new street light or traffic foundation is needed may take longer to resolve.

File a Complaint

To file a complaint, you must provide:

  • A location of the street light condition
  • Contact information (name, phone number, and email address)

Use the Street Lighting Repair Form to report a streetlight condition.

Check Status of a Complaint

Check the status of a streetlight Service Request.

 

Orange Light Over Luminaire

Orange lights over luminaires designate the location or intersection with fire or police alarm call boxes.

Follow Up on Street Light Outages

To get information about a street light that has been out for more than 90 days, contact the appropriate Borough Commissioner Office.

Section.Name: Report an Item on a Pole or Wire
Section.Content:
Streetlights

Streetlights have metal poles and are usually powered by energy supplied through wiring located in the base at the bottom of the pole. They are rarely powered by wires strung between poles. 

Streetlights are maintained by the Department of Transportation (DOT). DOT does not take reports of items hanging from streetlights because they do not prevent the light from working.

Utility Poles

Utility poles are usually made of wood and have wires between them.

Utility poles are owned and maintained by the utility companies that provide electrical, telephone, or cable services:

  • Con Edison
  • Spectrum
  • Verizon

To report problems or potential safety hazards with electrical poles or wires, contact the utility companies. NYC311 does not know which company owns specific poles or wires.
